sanskrit: hemarūpyapramṛṣṭānāṃ vāsasāṃ śilpinirmitāḥ nānāvarṇā rathe bhānti śvasanena prakampitāḥ
english: Wrought by craftsmen from cloths burnished with gold and silver, hangings of many hues gleam upon the chariot, trembling as the wind sets them astir.

sanskrit: sahemacandratārārkāḥ patākāḥ kiṅkiṇīyutāḥ paśya karṇārjunasyaitāḥ saudāminya ivāmbude
english: Behold these banners, hung with little bells and bearing emblems of the golden moon, the stars, and the sun—they flash, O Karṇa, on Arjuna's car like streaks of lightning in a thundercloud.

sanskrit: dhvajāḥ kaṇakaṇāyante vātenābhisamīritāḥ sapatākā rathāś cāpi pāñcālānāṃ mahātmanām
english: The standards jangle and chime, driven by the wind, and the chariots too, with their pennons, belong to the high-souled Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: nāgāśvarathapattyaughāṃs tāvakān samabhighnataḥ dhvajāgraṃ dṛśyate tv asya jyāśabdaś cāpi śrūyate
english: As he smites the flood of your elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers, the tip of his banner can be seen, and the twang of his bowstring is heard.

sanskrit: adya draṣṭāsi taṃ vīraṃ śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim nighnantaṃ śātravān saṃkhye yaṃ karṇa paripṛcchasi
english: Today, Karṇa, you shall behold that hero of the white horses, whose charioteer is Kṛṣṇa, striking down his foes in battle—the very warrior of whom you keep asking.

sanskrit: adya tau puruṣavyāghrau lohitākṣau paraṃtapau vāsudevārjunau karṇa draṣṭāsy ekarathasthitau
english: Today, Karṇa, you shall see those two tigers among men, red-eyed scorchers of the foe, Vāsudeva and Arjuna, standing together upon a single car.

sanskrit: sārathir yasya vārṣṇeyo gāṇḍīvaṃ yasya kārmukam taṃ ced dhantāsi rādheya tvaṃ no rājā bhaviṣyasi
english: He whose charioteer is the Vārṣṇeya and whose bow is the Gāṇḍīva—if you can slay him, O Rādheya, you shall become our king.

sanskrit: eṣa saṃśaptakāhūtas tān evābhimukho gataḥ karoti kadanaṃ caiṣāṃ saṃgrāme dviṣatāṃ balī iti bruvāṇaṃ madreśaṃ karṇaḥ prāhātimanyumān
english: "Summoned by the Saṃśaptakas, he has gone straight to meet them, and that mighty one wreaks havoc upon those foes in the fray"—so spoke the lord of the Madras, and Karṇa, full of furious wrath, answered him.

sanskrit: paśya saṃśaptakaiḥ kruddhaiḥ sarvataḥ samabhidrutaḥ eṣa sūrya ivāmbhodaiś channaḥ pārtho na dṛśyate etad anto 'rjunaḥ śalya nimagnaḥ śokasāgare
english: Look—beset on every side by the enraged Saṃśaptakas, the son of Pṛthā is no more to be seen, veiled as the sun is veiled by clouds. This is his end, O Śalya: Arjuna has sunk in an ocean of sorrow.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca varuṇaṃ ko 'mbhasā hanyād indhanena ca pāvakam ko vānilaṃ nigṛhṇīyāt pibed vā ko mahārṇavam
english: Śalya said: Who could slay Varuṇa with water, or the fire with fuel? Who could fetter the wind, or who could drink up the great ocean?

sanskrit: īdṛg rūpam ahaṃ manye pārthasya yudhi nigraham na hi śakyo 'rjuno jetuṃ sendraiḥ sarvaiḥ surāsuraiḥ
english: Such, I deem, would be the subduing of Pṛthā's son in battle. For Arjuna cannot be conquered by all the gods and demons together, with Indra at their head.

sanskrit: athaivaṃ paritoṣas te vācoktvā sumanā bhava na sa śakyo yudhā jetum anyaṃ kuru manoratham
english: Yet if it pleases you to be so deluded, speak on and be of good cheer; but he cannot be conquered in war—set your heart upon some other wish.

sanskrit: bāhubhyām uddhared bhūmiṃ dahet kruddha imāḥ prajāḥ pātayet tridivād devān yo 'rjunaṃ samare jayet
english: He who could vanquish Arjuna in battle could lift up the earth with his two arms, could in his wrath burn up these creatures, could cast down the gods from the third heaven.

sanskrit: paśya kuntīsutaṃ vīraṃ bhīmam akliṣṭakāriṇam prabhāsantaṃ mahābāhuṃ sthitaṃ merum ivācalam
english: Behold the hero, Kuntī's son Bhīma, who toils untiringly, the mighty-armed one blazing in his splendor, standing immovable as Mount Meru.

sanskrit: amarṣī nityasaṃrabdhaś ciraṃ vairam anusmaran eṣa bhīmo jayaprepsur yudhi tiṣṭhati vīryavān
english: Impatient of insult, ever seething, nursing his long grudge, here stands the valiant Bhīma in the fight, athirst for victory.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tiṣṭhaty asukaraḥ saṃkhye paraiḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Here stands the best of the upholders of righteousness, the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, hard for foes to withstand in battle, that conqueror of the cities of his enemies.

sanskrit: etau ca puruṣavyāghrāv aśvināv iva sodarau nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca tiṣṭhato yudhi durjayau
english: And here stand those two tigers among men, brothers like the twin Aśvins—Nakula and Sahadeva—unconquerable in the fight.

sanskrit: dṛśyanta ete kārṣṇeyāḥ pañca pañcācalā iva vyavasthitā yotsyamānāḥ sarve 'rjunasamā yudhi
english: Yonder are seen these five sons of Kṛṣṇā, arrayed for war like five mountains, each one Arjuna's equal in the field.

sanskrit: ete drupadaputrāś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ hīnāḥ satyajitā vīrās tiṣṭhanti paramaujasaḥ
english: And here are the sons of Drupada, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head—heroes of surpassing might, though bereft now of Satyajit—holding their ground.

sanskrit: iti saṃvadator eva tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ te sene samasajjetāṃ gaṅgāyamunavad bhṛśam
english: Even as those two lions among men were thus conversing, the two armies clashed violently together, like the Gaṅgā meeting the Yamunā.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu saṃsakteṣu ca saṃjaya saṃśaptakān kathaṃ pārtho gataḥ karṇaś ca pāṇḍavān
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the hosts were thus arrayed and locked in conflict, O Saṃjaya, how did the son of Pṛthā go against the Saṃśaptakas, and Karṇa against the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: etad vistarato yuddhaṃ prabrūhi kuśalo hy asi na hi tṛpyāmi vīrāṇāṃ śṛṇvāno vikramān raṇe
english: Tell me this battle in full, for you are skilled in the telling; I never tire of hearing the valorous deeds of heroes in the fray.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tat sthāne samavasthāpya pratyamitraṃ mahābalam avyūhatārjuno vyūhaṃ putrasya tava durnaye
english: Saṃjaya said: Having stationed his mighty army in its place to face the foe, Arjuna marshalled a battle-array against your son's ill counsel.

sanskrit: tat sādināgakalilaṃ padātirathasaṃkulam dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhair vyūḍham aśobhata mahad balam
english: Thick with horsemen and elephants, crowded with foot and chariots, that great host, arrayed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the other leaders, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: pārāvatasavarṇāśvaś candrādityasamadyutiḥ pārṣataḥ prababhau dhanvī kālo vigrahavān iva
english: With horses dove-grey in hue, and splendor like the moon's and the sun's, the son of Pṛṣata, bow in hand, blazed forth like Death himself made flesh.

sanskrit: pārṣataṃ tv abhi saṃtasthur draupadeyā yuyutsavaḥ sānugā bhīmavapuṣaś candraṃ tārāgaṇā iva
english: About the son of Pṛṣata stood the sons of Draupadī, eager for battle, dread of aspect, with their followers, as the host of stars about the moon.

sanskrit: atha vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu prekṣya saṃśaptakān raṇe kruddho 'rjuno 'bhidudrāva vyākṣipan gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ
english: Then, when the hosts were marshalled, Arjuna, beholding the Saṃśaptakas on the field, rushed upon them in wrath, brandishing the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: atha saṃśaptakāḥ pārtham abhyadhāvan vadhaiṣiṇaḥ vijaye kṛtasaṃkalpā mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Then the Saṃśaptakas charged at Pṛthā's son, athirst to slay, resolved upon victory, having made death their only turning-back.

sanskrit: tad aśvasaṃghabahulaṃ mattanāgarathākulam pattimac chūravīraughair drutam arjunam ādravat
english: That force, teeming with troops of horse, thronged with rutting elephants and chariots, dense with footmen and floods of brave warriors, rushed swiftly upon Arjuna.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulas teṣām āsīt kirīṭinā tasyaiva naḥ śruto yādṛṅ nivātakavacaiḥ saha
english: The tumultuous clash between them and the Diademed One was such as we had heard of in his fight against the Nivātakavacas.

sanskrit: rathān aśvān dhvajān nāgān pattīn rathapatīn api iṣūn dhanūṃṣi khaḍgāṃś ca cakrāṇi ca paraśvadhān
english: Chariots, horses, banners, elephants, foot-soldiers, and lords of chariots, arrows, bows, swords, discuses, and battle-axes—

sanskrit: sāyudhān udyatān bāhūn udyatāny āyudhāni ca ciccheda dviṣatāṃ pārthaḥ śirāṃsi ca sahasraśaḥ
english: —and arms upraised with their weapons, and weapons held aloft, and heads of his foes by the thousand, the son of Pṛthā cut asunder.

sanskrit: tasmin sainye mahāvarte pātālāvartasaṃnibhe nimagnaṃ taṃ rathaṃ matvā neduḥ saṃśaptakā mudā
english: Thinking his chariot sunk in that great whirlpool of an army, like the whirlpool of the nether deep, the Saṃśaptakas roared aloud for joy.

sanskrit: sa purastād arīn hatvā paścārdhenottareṇa ca dakṣiṇena ca bībhatsuḥ kruddho rudraḥ paśūn iva
english: But Bībhatsu in his wrath slew his foes before him, and with the rear and the north and the south of his car as well, like Rudra slaughtering the beasts.

sanskrit: atha pāñcālacedīnāṃ sṛñjayānāṃ ca māriṣa tvadīyaiḥ saha saṃgrāma āsīt paramadāruṇaḥ
english: Then, O venerable one, between the Pāñcālas, the Cedis, and the Sṛñjayas and your warriors there raged a most terrible battle.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ hṛṣṭasenāḥ susaṃrabdhā rathānīkaiḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman, and Śakuni the son of Subala, their troops exultant and furious, smiting hard with their hosts of chariots—

sanskrit: kosalaiḥ kāśimatsyaiś ca kārūṣaiḥ kekayair api śūrasenaiḥ śūravīrair yuyudhur yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: —battle-maddened, they fought against the Kosalas, the Kāśis, the Matsyas, the Karūṣas, the Kekayas, and the brave Śūrasenas, valiant warriors all.

sanskrit: teṣām antakaraṃ yuddhaṃ dehapāpmapraṇāśanam śūdraviṭkṣatravīrāṇāṃ dharmyaṃ svargyaṃ yaśaskaram
english: That fight, which made an end of them, destroyed the sins of their bodies; for those warriors—Śūdra, Vaiśya, and Kṣatriya—it was righteous, heaven-winning, and bestowing fame.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi sahito bhrātṛbhir bharatarṣabha guptaḥ kurupravīraiś ca madrāṇāṃ ca mahārathaiḥ
english: Duryodhana too, O bull of the Bharatas, together with his brothers, guarded by the foremost Kuru heroes and the great car-warriors of the Madras,

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaiḥ sahapāñcālaiś cedibhiḥ sātyakena ca yudhyamānaṃ raṇe karṇaṃ kuruvīro 'bhyapālayat
english: —that Kuru hero shielded Karṇa as he fought in the field against the Pāṇḍavas with the Pāñcālas, the Cedis, and Sātyaki.

sanskrit: karṇo 'pi niśitair bāṇair vinihatya mahācamūm pramṛdya ca rathaśreṣṭhān yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat
english: And Karṇa too, smiting down the great host with his sharpened arrows and crushing the foremost car-warriors, sorely beset Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vipatrāyudhadehāsūn kṛtvā śatrūn sahasraśaḥ yuktvā svargayaśobhyāṃ ca svebhyo mudam udāvahat
english: Stripping his foes by the thousand of their armor, their weapons, their bodies, and their breath, and joining them to heaven and to fame, he brought joy to his own.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yat tat praviśya pārthānāṃ senāṃ kurvañ janakṣayam karṇo rājānam abhyarcchat tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How Karṇa, having pierced the army of the sons of Pṛthā and wrought slaughter among men, fell upon the king—tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: ke ca pravīrāḥ pārthānāṃ yudhi karṇam avārayan kāṃś ca pramathyādhirathir yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat
english: Which heroes of the Pārthas held Karṇa back in the fight? And whom did the son of Adhiratha crush before he beset Yudhiṣṭhira?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhān pārthān dṛṣṭvā karṇo vyavasthitān samabhyadhāvat tvaritaḥ pāñcālāñ śatrukarśanaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the Pārthas arrayed with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, Karṇa, the harrower of foes, charged swiftly upon the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: taṃ tūrṇam abhidhāvantaṃ pāñcālā jitakāśinaḥ pratyudyayur mahārāja haṃsā iva mahārṇavam
english: As he rushed swiftly on, the Pāñcālas, flushed with the look of victory, went forth to meet him, O great king, like wild geese flying toward the mighty ocean.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhasahasrāṇāṃ nisvano hṛdayaṃgamaḥ prādurāsīd ubhayato bherīśabdaś ca dāruṇaḥ
english: Then on both sides arose the heart-stirring blast of a thousand conches and the terrible thunder of war-drums.

sanskrit: nānāvāditranādaś ca dvipāśvarathanisvanaḥ siṃhanādaś ca vīrāṇām abhavad dāruṇas tadā
english: And the sound of many instruments, the clamor of elephants, horses, and chariots, and the lions' roar of the heroes grew terrible in that hour.

sanskrit: sādridrumārṇavā bhūmiḥ savātāmbudam ambaram sārkendugrahanakṣatrā dyauś ca vyaktaṃ vyaghūrṇata
english: The earth with its mountains, trees, and seas, the sky with its winds and clouds, and the heaven with its sun, moon, planets, and stars—all visibly reeled.

sanskrit: ati bhūtāni taṃ śabdaṃ menire 'ti ca vivyathuḥ yāni cāplavasattvāni prāyas tāni mṛtāni ca
english: Living things were overwhelmed by that uproar and were sore afflicted; and of the creatures that could not swim, the most part perished.

sanskrit: atha karṇo bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ śīghram astram udīrayan jaghāna pāṇḍavīṃ senām āsurīṃ maghavān iva
english: Then Karṇa, exceedingly wrathful, loosing his weapons swiftly, smote the Pāṇḍava army as Maghavat smote the host of demons.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavarathāṃs tūrṇaṃ praviśya visṛjañ śarān prabhadrakāṇāṃ pravarān ahanat saptasaptatim
english: Swiftly piercing among the Pāṇḍava chariots and loosing his shafts, he slew seventy and seven of the foremost of the Prabhadrakas.

sanskrit: tataḥ supuṅkhair niśitai rathaśreṣṭho ratheṣubhiḥ avadhīt pañcaviṃśatyā pāñcālān pañcaviṃśatim
english: Then that best of car-warriors, with twenty-five fair-feathered, whetted chariot-arrows, slew five and twenty Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair nārācaiḥ parakāyavidāraṇaiḥ cedikān avadhīd vīraḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: With gold-feathered iron shafts that cleave through the bodies of foes, the hero slew the Cedis by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā samare karma kurvāṇam atimānuṣam parivavrur mahārāja pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajāḥ
english: As he wrought thus in battle his more-than-human deeds, O great king, the chariot-throngs of the Pāñcālas hemmed him round.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhāya viśikhān pañca bhārata duḥsahān pāñcālān avadhīt pañca karṇo vaikartano vṛṣaḥ
english: Then fitting five unbearable shafts to his bow, O Bhārata, Karṇa Vaikartana, the bull among men, slew five Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: bhānudevaṃ citrasenaṃ senābinduṃ ca bhārata tapanaṃ śūrasenaṃ ca pāñcālān avadhīd raṇe
english: Bhānudeva, Citrasena, and Senābindu, O Bhārata, and Tapana and Śūrasena—these Pāñcālas he slew in the fray.

sanskrit: pāñcāleṣu ca śūreṣu vadhyamāneṣu sāyakaiḥ hāhākāro mahān āsīt pāñcālānāṃ mahāhave
english: As the brave Pāñcālas were being struck down by his arrows, a great wail of woe arose among the Pāñcālas in that mighty battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃkīryamāṇānāṃ hāhākārakṛtā diśaḥ punar eva ca tān karṇo jaghānāśu patatribhiḥ
english: As they were scattered in rout, the quarters were filled with their cries of woe; and again Karṇa swiftly slew them with his feathered shafts.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣau tu karṇasya putrau māriṣa durjayau suṣeṇaḥ satyasenaś ca tyaktvā prāṇān ayudhyatām
english: Now the guards of Karṇa's chariot-wheels were his two sons, O venerable one, hard to conquer—Suṣeṇa and Satyasena—who fought, having staked their very lives.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhagopas tu karṇasya jyeṣṭhaḥ putro mahārathaḥ vṛṣasenaḥ svayaṃ karṇaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ paryapālayat
english: And the guard of Karṇa's rear was his eldest son, the great car-warrior Vṛṣasena, who himself protected Karṇa from behind.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ sātyakiś ca draupadeyā vṛkodaraḥ janamejayaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca pravīrāś ca prabhadrakāḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Sātyaki, the sons of Draupadī, Vṛkodara, Janamejaya and Śikhaṇḍin, and the heroic Prabhadrakas,

sanskrit: cedikekayapāñcālā yamau matsyāś ca daṃśitāḥ samabhyadhāvan rādheyaṃ jighāṃsantaḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: the Cedis, Kekayas, and Pāñcālas, the twins and the Matsyas, all mailed and smiting hard, charged upon Rādheya, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ vividhaiḥ śastraiḥ śaradhārābhir eva ca abhyavarṣan vimṛdnantaḥ prāvṛṣīvāmbudā girim
english: With weapons of every kind and with showers of arrows they rained upon him, crushing him, as in the rainy season the clouds beat upon a mountain.

sanskrit: pitaraṃ tu parīpsantaḥ karṇaputrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ tvadīyāś cāpare rājan vīrā vīrān avārayan
english: But Karṇa's sons, smiting fiercely, sought to save their father, and your other heroes too, O king, held those heroes back.

sanskrit: suṣeṇo bhīmasenasya chittvā bhallena kārmukam nārācaiḥ saptabhir viddhvā hṛdi bhīmaṃ nanāda ha
english: Suṣeṇa, having cut Bhīmasena's bow with a broad-headed shaft and pierced Bhīma in the breast with seven iron arrows, let out a roar.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sudṛḍhaṃ bhīmavikramaḥ sajyaṃ vṛkodaraḥ kṛtvā suṣeṇasyācchinad dhanuḥ
english: Then Vṛkodara of dread prowess, taking up another stout bow and stringing it, cut asunder Suṣeṇa's bow.

sanskrit: vivyādha cainaṃ navabhiḥ kruddho nṛtyann iveṣubhiḥ karṇaṃ ca tūrṇaṃ vivyādha trisaptatyā śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And in his wrath, as though dancing, he pierced him with nine arrows, and swiftly pierced Karṇa too with three and seventy whetted shafts.

sanskrit: satyasenaṃ ca daśabhiḥ sāśvasūtadhvajāyudham paśyatāṃ suhṛdāṃ madhye karṇaputram apātayat
english: And Satyasena, Karṇa's son, with his horses, his charioteer, his banner, and his weapons, he struck down with ten shafts in the very midst of his beholding friends.

sanskrit: kṣurapraṇunnaṃ tat tasya śiraś candranibhānanam śubhadarśanam evāsīn nālabhraṣṭam ivāmbujam
english: His head, struck off by the razor-arrow, its face fair as the moon, was lovely still to look upon, like a lotus fallen from its stalk.

sanskrit: hatvā karṇasutaṃ bhīmas tāvakān punar ārdayat kṛpahārdikyayoś chittvā cāpe tāv apy athārdayat
english: Having slain Karṇa's son, Bhīma fell once more upon your men; and severing the bows of Kṛpa and the son of Hṛdika, he afflicted those two as well.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ tribhir viddhvā śakuniṃ ṣaḍbhir āyasaiḥ ulūkaṃ ca patatriṃ ca cakāra virathāv ubhau
english: Piercing Duḥśāsana with three and Śakuni with six iron shafts, he made both Ulūka and Patatrin chariotless.

sanskrit: he suṣeṇa hato 'sīti bruvann ādatta sāyakam tam asya karṇaś ciccheda tribhiś cainam atāḍayat
english: "Ho, Suṣeṇa, you are slain!"—so crying, he took up an arrow; but Karṇa cut it down and struck him with three shafts.

sanskrit: athānyam api jagrāha suparvāṇaṃ sutejanam suṣeṇāyāsṛjad bhīmas tam apy asyācchinad vṛṣaḥ
english: Then Bhīma seized yet another, well-jointed and keenly sharpened, and loosed it at Suṣeṇa; but that one too the bull-like Karṇa cut down.

sanskrit: punaḥ karṇas trisaptatyā bhīmasenaṃ ratheṣubhiḥ putraṃ parīpsan vivyādha krūraṃ krūrair jighāṃsayā
english: Again Karṇa, seeking to save his son, pierced the cruel Bhīmasena with three and seventy chariot-arrows, fierce shafts loosed in his desire to kill.

sanskrit: suṣeṇas tu dhanur gṛhya bhārasādhanam uttamam nakulaṃ pañcabhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: And Suṣeṇa, seizing an excellent bow that could bear a heavy strain, smote Nakula with five arrows in the arms and the breast.

sanskrit: nakulas taṃ tu viṃśatyā viddhvā bhārasahair dṛḍhaiḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ karṇasya bhayam ādadhat
english: But Nakula, piercing him in turn with twenty stout, strain-bearing shafts, let out a mighty roar that struck fear into Karṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ suṣeṇo mahārāja viddhvā daśabhir āśugaiḥ ciccheda ca dhanuḥ śīghraṃ kṣurapreṇa mahārathaḥ
english: Then Suṣeṇa, O great king, that great car-warrior, having pierced him with ten swift arrows, quickly cut his bow with a razor-shaft.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya nakulaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ suṣeṇaṃ bahubhir bāṇair vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Then Nakula, beside himself with wrath, took up another bow and held Suṣeṇa back in the encounter with many arrows.

sanskrit: sa tu bāṇair diśo rājann ācchādya paravīrahā ājaghne sārathiṃ cāsya suṣeṇaṃ ca tatas tribhiḥ ciccheda cāsya sudṛḍhaṃ dhanur bhallais tribhis tridhā
english: And that slayer of hostile heroes, O king, covering the quarters with his arrows, smote his charioteer, and then struck Suṣeṇa with three shafts, and cut his stout bow in three with three broad-headed arrows.
